In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the epigenome plays a key role in DLBCL pathophysiology.
SMAD1 expression in DLBCL can be reactivated with the demethylation drug decitabine and this leads to increased apoptosis and decreased tumor growth.
SMAD1 expression is epigenetically regulated in DLBCL, that SMAD1 is a tumor suppressor in DLBCL and that the pharmacologic re-expression of SMAD1 by DAC has a tumor suppressive effect in DLBCL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TGF-beta signaling pathway is blocked by hypermethylation in DLBCL and the restoration of SMAD expression by demethylating agents can restore the tumor suppressive function of TGF-beta signaling.

the S1P receptor S1PR1 and the TGF- β signaling pathway are both silenced in DLBCL and that the pharmacologic restoration of S1PR1 expression and SMAD1 expression in DLBCL cells by decitabine, a DNA demethylating agent, sensitizes DLBCL cells to S1P- and TGF-β-mediated apoptosis.

the TGFβ/SMAD1/S1PR2 axis in DLBCL cells is inactivated by hypermethylation and that the restoration of SMAD expression by the demethylation drug DAC restores the tumor suppressive effects of this signaling axis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
epigenetic reprogramming of DLBCL cells with the demethylating drug DAC restores the tumor suppressive TGF-β/SMAD1 axis and may provide an effective therapeutic option for DLBCL.
epigenetic reprogramming is an effective strategy to reverse the pathologic phenotype in DLBCL.
epigenetic drugs may be used to reverse the epigenetic changes associated with DLBCL pathophysiology, thereby restoring the tumor suppressive function of the TGF- β/SMAD1 pathway in DLBLC.
